# idigdata

> Independent practice for business-system transformation. Embedded transformation leadership for $100M–$1B operators in the agentic era. Founded 2016 by Robert Paddock.

idigdata is the independent practice of Robert Paddock — a 30-year business-system transformation operator who embeds inside mid-market businesses ($100M–$1B revenue), owns the transformation path above the vendors, installs a business-owned operating asset, and exits by design when the business can carry the result. Three industry specialties: architecture-engineering-construction (AEC), beverage consumer packaged goods (CPG), and healthcare. System breadth covers ERP, WMS, MES, EMR, LIMS, QMS, CPQ, CRM, MDM, and HRIS, with a Common Data Model and master-data discipline under every engagement.

## The problem idigdata owns

Bain finds 88% of business transformations fall short of their ambitions, and Stanford's Digital Economy Lab finds the same bottleneck in the AI version: the technology works; delivery is where it dies. The market is full of diagnosers who explain the failure, vendors who implement a slice, and AI builders who rent tools on their own state — but none of them owns the transformation as a business system. idigdata is the missing third: a senior operator who embeds, builds, transfers, and exits, accountable for getting the work to done/done.

## Key Substance

**Model — embedded transformation leadership.** Robert Paddock works inside the business at senior-operator altitude, owns the transformation path above the vendors, develops the people who will carry the result, and leaves a business-owned operating asset. Fractional, adoption, and recovery are entry modes into the same model. Vendor-agnostic. No carried bench, no managed-services tail, no lock-in. Exit-by-design.

**Decision integrity (production agentics).** Agentics is the accelerant on a 30-year operator spine, not the headline. Putting agents into production turns on two questions: can the business safely HOLD them (governed data, a shared version of reality, clear ownership of what an agent can touch) and can it ABSORB them (people who delegate, verify, and own output; workflows redesigned around the work; a human on every consequential call). Answer both and agentic capability becomes decision integrity — decisions the business can stand behind, trace, and defend; defensible by design. Robert's first two calls are to the CFO and the Compliance Officer, because they carry the consequences.

**Three-system delivery architecture.** Rig — the governed build estate that carries build plans, source checks, write discipline, acceptance gates, tests, observable agent work, and CI/CD. BOSS — the business process harness: a client-owned tier-2 operating fabric above ERP, CRM, HRIS, data, and specialty systems, modeling processes, owners, controls, decisions, delivery state, SOP memory, and green/green validation. FlowCraft — the org and instance framework that turns owned operating models into runnable human and agentic workflows. DigOps is idigdata's live FlowCraft instance and reference proof at practice scale.

**Six Process Constellations.** The operating-process spine across every transformation: P2P (procure to pay), O2C (order to cash), P2M (plan to make), S2S (systems to support), D2R (data to report), MDM (master data management). Same six in every install; the makeup differs per operator.

**System breadth.** ERP, WMS, MES, EMR, LIMS, QMS, CPQ, CRM, MDM, HRIS. Platforms in active rotation: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, Dynamics NAV, Salesforce, SAP, Snowflake, Databricks, Power BI. Common Data Model and master-data discipline thread through every engagement.

**Proof.** 30 years in business-system transformation; 50+ implementations across AEC, beverage CPG, and healthcare; 15 full transformations at scale, led end-to-end; $100M–$1B operators; agentics in production. The proof is the arc and the live systems, not a count.

**Capital and ownership logic.** A meaningful transformation is defensible as a capital investment — build work creates an owned asset; go-live begins the useful-life conversation. The model is structurally lean: the business owns the asset and the exit is designed into the work. Rig, BOSS, and FlowCraft are free/client-owned software architecture rather than a subscription trap; BOSS and FlowCraft client instances are delivered as part of the owned asset. The paid work is the embedded operator build, transfer, training, support path, maintenance path, and CI/CD capability, including trained human operators and actual agents.

## Buyer profile

Mid-market operators, $100M–$1B revenue, with multi-entity, multi-platform, vendor-heavy environments across ERP, WMS, MES, EMR, CRM/CPQ, LIMS, QMS, MDM, or HRIS — strongest pattern matches in AEC, beverage CPG, and healthcare. The buyer wants to lead with technology, land the work in the operating business, and own the result instead of renting dependency. Recognizes stalled ERP runs, the vendor-partner trap, SOPs that drift, transformation treated as cost rather than asset, and AI pilots that demo well and fail in operations.
